html:
A bank in Istanbul that acted as the state bank of the Ottoman Empire from 1863. It was owned by British and French investors.

It began in 1856 as a small British bank, at a time when the empire had started borrowing in Europe to pay for the Crimean War. In 1863 British and French capital joined to refound it as the Imperial Ottoman Bank, with a charter from the sultan. It issued the empire's banknotes, handled its accounts and arranged its foreign loans, and it opened branches across the Balkans, Anatolia and the Arab provinces. By 1900 it was the largest bank in the empire.

The bank stood at the centre of the empire's money troubles. When the state stopped paying its debts in 1875, the bank helped work out the deal that set up the Ottoman Public Debt Administration in 1881.

In 1896 armed members of the Armenian Revolutionary Federation seized its Istanbul head office to draw Europe's eyes to attacks on Armenians; mob violence against Armenians in the city followed. The bank outlived the empire and worked in the Turkish Republic as the Ottoman Bank until it merged into another bank in 2001.
sum: A bank in Istanbul that acted as the state bank of the Ottoman Empire from 1863. It was owned by British and French investors.
